title: Beyond Equilibrium Raman Thermometry: Fermi-Level Control of the Anti-Stokes Response in Graphene
authors: Martin Jindra, Luka Pirker, Tim Verhagen, Ciarán Fowley, Martin Kalbáč, Matěj Velický, † Riichiro Saito, Ado Jorio, Otakar Frank
abstract: Non-equilibrium electron and phonon populations govern heat generation and dissipation in nanoscale devices, yet their direct characterization remains challenging. Anti-Stokes Raman scattering provides a sensitive probe of phonon populations and local temperatures, although its interpretation becomes more complex when electronic and phononic populations are driven out of equilibrium. Here, we investigate the gate-dependent anti-Stokes Raman response of monolayer graphene and find that the anti-Stokes response deviates from that expected from an equilibrium phonon population. Using a spatially localized microdroplet spectroelectrochemical platform, dielectric back-gates, and chemical doping, we observe a strong and reversible suppression of the G-mode anti-Stokes intensity as the Fermi level is tuned away from the Dirac point, while the Stokes intensity remains essentially unchanged. By contrast, the G-mode frequency and linewidth of both the Stokes and anti-Stokes branches evolve with doping as expected from the established Kohn-anomaly picture. The anti-Stokes/Stokes intensity ratio decreases by several-fold over the measured range and displays a pronounced, gate-dependent power response with maximum sensitivity at charge neutrality. Comparison with previous studies of non-equilibrium carrier dynamics in doped graphene suggests an important role of Fermi-level-dependent electronic phase space, which can influence both hot-carrier-driven phonon populations and electronically mediated Stokes-anti-Stokes scattering. Our findings establish anti-Stokes Raman scattering as a sensitive probe of electron-phonon coupling and non-equilibrium phonon dynamics in graphene.
summary: This paper uses anti-Stokes Raman scattering on graphene to probe non-equilibrium electron-phonon dynamics. By tuning the Fermi level using advanced electrochemical gating, the authors show that the anti-Stokes signal is strongly suppressed away from the Dirac point, contradicting simple thermal models. This establishes the anti-Stokes response as a sensitive diagnostic tool for electronic state-dependent phonon coupling in nanoscale conductors.
main_problem: The study addresses the challenge of directly characterizing non-equilibrium electron and phonon populations that govern heat generation and dissipation in nanoscale electronic devices.
main_result: The anti-Stokes Raman response in graphene shows a strong, reversible, and gate-dependent suppression away from the Dirac point, indicating that the scattering process is significantly influenced by the electronic phase space rather than just the equilibrium phonon population.
method: The researchers utilized anti-Stokes Raman scattering spectroscopy, employing a microdroplet spectroelectrochemical platform combined with dielectric back-gates and chemical doping to tune the Fermi level ($E_F$) in monolayer graphene.
model_or_system: The physical system is monolayer graphene, whose electronic and vibrational properties are probed using Raman scattering. The analysis compares the measured anti-Stokes/Stokes intensity ratio against predictions based on equilibrium phonon populations, revealing deviations.
key_observables: Anti-Stokes/Stokes intensity ratio ($I_{aS}/I_S$), G-mode anti-Stokes and Stokes intensities, G-mode frequency and linewidth evolution, and the dependence of these observables on the gate-tuned Fermi level ($E_F$).
important_parameters: Fermi level ($E_F$), Dirac point (charge neutrality point), excitation power ($P$), and gate voltage ($V_G$).
main_assumptions: The standard interpretation of the anti-Stokes/Stokes ratio as a measure of lattice temperature is challenged by the observed gate-dependent deviations, suggesting a necessary inclusion of electronic contributions.
figures_summary: Figures show gate-dependent heatmaps of G bands, the breakdown of the standard thermometry interpretation, and the power dependence of the anti-Stokes/Stokes ratio, all demonstrating strong electronic control over the scattering signal.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of non-equilibrium characterization, details the experimental setup using advanced gating techniques, presents measurements showing the gate-dependent suppression of $I_{aS}$ while $I_S$ remains stable, and concludes by establishing the anti-Stokes response as a sensitive probe of electron-phonon coupling.
why_interesting: This work provides an experimental demonstration of how electronic structure (Fermi level) can fundamentally alter phonon scattering signatures, which is relevant to understanding energy dissipation in quantum devices and open quantum systems.
